extracted.intended_audience: journalism students and reporters (especially police/crime beat reporters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting and writing police and crime news: how to select, arrange, and present facts so stories are accurate, fair, constructive, and appropriate in tone (informative, human-interest, or dramatic) while considering reader impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider effect on the reader / deterrent purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: In no other kind of news should the effect of the story on the reader receive more careful consideration than in news of crime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To have a deterrent effect, the crime must be shown to be wrong; emphasize results of wrongdoing (legal punishment, remorse, pangs of guilty conscience, disgrace brought to others) so readers are discouraged from emulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive presentation emphasizing causes and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive presentation of crime news may include emphasis on underlying causes and responsibility, especially when these can be traced to bad conditions in the community or in society as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the criminal is a victim of circumstances, it may be legitimate to create sympathetic understanding; such emphasis leads readers to consider the necessity for changing conditions that contributed to the crime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sentimental treatment that creates undeserved sympathy
rubrics_metrics.description: A danger in writing stories of crime lies in creating sympathy for the undeserving wrong-doer by a sentimental treatment of him and his act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make more or less of a hero of the wrong-doer; avoid portrayals that lead undiscriminating readers to regard the crime as worthy of emulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not sacrifice truth or accuracy for picturesqueness or drama
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a temptation in writing crime stories to sacrifice truth and accuracy of detail in order to secure greater picturesqueness or stronger dramatic situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such treatment is an indefensible deviation from the fundamental duty of presenting the news fairly and accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence should come from factual selection and presentation (no moralizing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever influence a story of crime may have on the reader should be the result of the reporter's selection and presentation of the actual facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moralizing or 'editorializing' concerning the facts is unnecessary and undesirable in news stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose appropriate treatment/tone (informative, human-interest, humorous)
rubrics_metrics.description: Police news ranges widely; the purely informative story is often sufficient, but the strong personal element allows effective human-interest presentation; amusing aspects of minor offenses can justify humorous treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match tone to material: use informative approach for straightforward facts, human-interest to highlight personal elements, and avoid humor or levity when it would undermine seriousness or deterrent aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dramatic narrative and vivid description when true to facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Dramatic narrative and vivid description, when true to the facts of the news, are both legitimate and commendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure such narrative remains faithful to verified facts; dramatic style must not compromise accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep consistently to one point of view in arrangement and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important to keep consistently to one point of view in arranging and presenting the details, particularly in constructive stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a coherent narrative perspective so the story's emphasis and interpretation remain clear and not confusing or contradictory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use available primary material to make narration effective
rubrics_metrics.description: Available material for making the narration and the description effective includes confessions, interviews with witnesses and persons involved, and clues to the identity of the perpetrator or to the solution of any mysterious phases of the crime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on direct sources (confessions, interviews, clues) to support descriptive and narrative elements rather than speculation or invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure fairness: give accused and accusers a hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Fairness requires that persons accused of wrong-doing as well as their accusers be given a hearing in news stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek and report responses from both sides; avoid one-sided presentations that deny accused persons opportunity to state their case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use qualifying language for accused until conviction
rubrics_metrics.description: A person accused of crime is not a criminal unless he has been convicted; until he has been found guilty, he is described as an 'alleged' criminal, or is said to be 'charged' with the crime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use terms like 'alleged' or 'charged' to avoid asserting guilt before legal determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report number of lives destroyed or endangered
rubrics_metrics.description: (Contents) number of lives destroyed or endangered
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear facts about casualties or danger to life as a primary element of significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report names of victims
rubrics_metrics.description: (Contents) names of victims
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide identities of victims when appropriate and verified, being mindful of privacy and sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report names of persons charged with the crime
rubrics_metrics.description: (Contents) names of persons charged with the crime
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify those charged, using qualifying language if not yet convicted; verify identity before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report arrests of suspects and detention of witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: (Contents) arrests of suspects and detention of witnesses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail law-enforcement actions such as arrests and witness detention to convey progress in the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report clues to the identity of the perpetrators when unknown
rubrics_metrics.description: (Contents) clues to the identity of the perpetrators when these are not known
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include investigative leads or clues that could explain or resolve the crime, without speculating beyond evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report causes, motives, and responsibility (known or conjectured)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Contents) causes, motives, and responsibility, known or conjectured
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain known or reasonably supported theories of motive or responsibility; distinguish fact from conjecture and avoid unfounded blame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report amount and character of loss
rubrics_metrics.description: (Contents) amount and character of loss
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide figures and descriptions of financial or material loss where relevant and verifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report methods employed in commission of the crime
rubrics_metrics.description: (Contents) methods employed in commission of the crime
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how the crime was carried out to inform readers and potentially aid prevention or investigation, being careful not to provide 'how-to' details that could enable copycats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report measures to prevent similar crimes
rubrics_metrics.description: (Contents) measures to prevent similar crimes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include information on prevention steps, law-enforcement responses, or community measures that address underlying causes or reduce recurrence.
